questions.stem: What must be conserved in every nuclear equation?

options.text: The number of electrons only
Both mass number and atomic number
The chemical properties of the element
The number of neutrons only

questions.explanation: In every nuclear equation, the total mass number (nucleon number) and the total atomic number (proton number) must balance on both sides. This reflects conservation of nucleons and charge.

questions.stem: When a nucleus emits an alpha particle, what happens to its mass number and atomic number?

options.text: Mass number decreases by 4, atomic number decreases by 2
Mass number stays the same, atomic number decreases by 2
Mass number decreases by 2, atomic number decreases by 4
Mass number increases by 4, atomic number increases by 2

questions.explanation: An alpha particle has mass number 4 and atomic number 2. When emitted, the parent nucleus loses 4 from its mass number and 2 from its atomic number, forming a new element.

questions.stem: When a nucleus undergoes beta decay, what happens to its atomic number?

options.text: It increases by 2
It decreases by 1
It stays the same
It increases by 1

questions.explanation: In beta decay, a neutron changes into a proton and an electron (the beta particle). The mass number stays the same, but the atomic number increases by 1 because there is now one more proton.

questions.stem: What effect does gamma emission have on the mass number and atomic number of a nucleus?

options.text: Mass number decreases by 4, atomic number decreases by 2
Mass number increases by 1, atomic number stays the same
Both mass number and atomic number decrease by 1
Neither mass number nor atomic number changes

questions.explanation: Gamma rays are electromagnetic radiation with no mass and no charge. When a nucleus emits gamma radiation, it loses energy but the mass number and atomic number remain unchanged.

questions.stem: Radium-226 (atomic number 88) undergoes alpha decay. What is the mass number and atomic number of the daughter nucleus?

options.text: Mass number 222, atomic number 86
Mass number 224, atomic number 87
Mass number 230, atomic number 90
Mass number 226, atomic number 86

questions.explanation: Alpha decay reduces the mass number by 4 (226 - 4 = 222) and the atomic number by 2 (88 - 2 = 86). The daughter nucleus is radon-222.

questions.stem: In a nuclear equation, what does the bottom number (subscript) represent?

options.text: The atomic number (number of protons)
The mass number
The number of electrons
The number of neutrons

questions.explanation: In nuclear notation, the bottom number (subscript) is the atomic number, which represents the number of protons. The top number (superscript) is the mass number, representing the total of protons and neutrons.

questions.stem: Does the element change when a nucleus undergoes beta decay?

options.text: Yes, because the atomic number increases by 1, creating a new element
No, the element stays the same because the mass number does not change
Yes, because the mass number decreases by 1
No, because only gamma emission changes the element

questions.explanation: Beta decay increases the atomic number by 1 (a neutron becomes a proton). Since the element is defined by its atomic number, the atom becomes a different element with one more proton.
